cards.front: Who said “That which does not kill us makes us stronger”?
Who said “Workers of the world, unite!”?
Who said “Two things fill the mind with ever new and increasing admiration and awe: the starry heavens above me and the moral law within me”?
Who said “Religion is the opium of the people”?
Who said “Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law”?
Who said “God is dead”?
Who said “The unexamined life is not worth living”?
Who said “Man is by nature a political animal”?
Who said “Hell is other people”?
Who said “You cannot step twice into the same river”?
Who said “Existence precedes essence”?
Who said “Everything flows”?
Who said “Plato is dear to me, but dearer still is truth”?
Who said “I know that I know nothing”?
Who said “He who fights with monsters should look to it that he himself does not become a monster”?
Who said “Happiness is not an ideal of reason but of imagination”?
Who said “The philosophers have only interpreted the world, in various ways; the point is to change it”?
Who said “I think, therefore I am”?
Who said “Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent”?
Who said “There is but one truly serious philosophical problem, and that is suicide”?
Who said “The heart has its reasons which reason knows nothing of”?
Who said “Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards”?
Who said “A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds”?
Who said “Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign”?
Who said “A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step”?
Who said “You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength”?
Who said “We suffer more often in imagination than in reality”?
Who said “It’s not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters”?
Who said “Our hearts are restless until they rest in You”?
Who said “No man is free who is not master of himself”?
Who said “Love, and do what you will”?
Who said “It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it”?
Who said “The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts”?
Who said “He who knows does not speak. He who speaks does not know”?
Who said “It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied”?
Who said “Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string”?
Who said “Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom”?
Who said “Man is but a reed, the weakest in nature, but he is a thinking reed”?
Who said “One must imagine Sisyphus happy”?
Who said “The limits of my language mean the limits of my world”?
Who said “Cogito, ergo sum”?
Who said “The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles”?
Who said “Dare to know! Have courage to use your own understanding!”?
Who said “Become who you are”?
Who said “The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing”?
Who said “All men by nature desire to know”?
Who said “Nothing endures but change”?
Who said “Man is condemned to be free”?
Who said “Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains”?
Who said “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman”?
Who said “Man is the measure of all things”?
Who said “The life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short”?
Who said “Reason is, and ought only to be the slave of the passions”?
Who said “What is rational is actual; and what is actual is rational”?
Who said “Life swings like a pendulum backward and forward between pain and boredom”?
Who said “The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation”?
Who said “The greatest happiness of the greatest number is the foundation of morals and legislation”?
Who said “Knowledge is power”?
Who said “No man's knowledge here can go beyond his experience”?
Who said “Language is the house of Being”?
Who said “The banality of evil”?
Who said “If God did not exist, it would be necessary to invent him”?
Who said “Que sais-je?”?
Who said “Am I a man who dreamt he was a butterfly, or a butterfly now dreaming he is a man?”?
Who said “The free man thinks of nothing less than of death”?
Who said “Science must begin with myths, and with the criticism of myths”?
Who said “The whole problem with the world is that fools and fanatics are always so certain of themselves, and wiser people so full of doubts”?
Who said “Entities should not be multiplied without necessity”?
Who said “Until philosophers are kings, or the kings and princes of this world have the spirit and power of philosophy, cities will never have rest from their evils”?
